s-13-opener.alt: One record from our systems atlas with the evidence it carries, each part numbered. A dark label reads Plausible, some evidence. Connection L02, in Loop R1, is named “Political spending can tilt policy toward donors”, and runs from Variable B1, money spent to influence politics, to Variable E1, policy advantages for wealthy and organized interests. A line, solid under its two delay ticks and dashed after them, carries a plus sign tag. Its words read Plausible, some evidence; sign plus, the two move the same way; delay M, 2 to 10 years. The source line names the atlas and the snapshot of October 15, 2026. A list beside it names the six numbered parts and their rules: the verb can, Rule 13.2; the grade word and gloss, Rule 13.3; the dashed line, Rule 13.4; the delay apart from the grade, Rule 13.5; the typed chip, Rule 13.9; the snapshot date, Rule 13.10.
s-13-opener.notes: Chapter 13's opener (D2-1708, D2-1732): a light drawing the chapter's rules use, with only the styles it needs. The line is the atlas build's own wire_marks; the numerals tie each part to the list (brand S1).

s-13-1-correct.alt: Four chart heads, one of each kind of evidence, each with a dark label, a grade line, a title, a measure line and a source. Finding, Documented: a Census Bureau survey: Child poverty stood at 13.4 percent in 2025 under the Supplemental Poverty Measure, with a note that defines the measure and gives the margin of error. Association, Well supported: Job postings offered 17 percent lower wages where a few employers did more of the hiring, with a note that the pattern does not show cause. Estimate, Well supported: Vehicle safety technologies saved an estimated 614,000 lives from 1960 to 2012, with a note on the agency’s method and its figure, 613,501. Illustration: A ranked bar puts the town with the most library hours first, labeled Illustrative data.
s-13-1-correct.notes: Evidence label and grade line as the approved chart system draws them (DR-52), with D3-83's grade rule for a public agency's survey. Child poverty from the engineer's census-spm-child-poverty file; its source line from the sidecar. CL1507 and DL06 read from the atlas.

s-13-1-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A chart head labeled Finding over the same study of job postings, titled Concentrated hiring cuts wages by 17 percent, with no note that the study measured a pattern.
s-13-1-failure.notes: Labeled failure: a causal verb and the Finding label over an association; grade line and source as the correct plate.

s-13-2-correct.alt: A table of five connections from our systems atlas, one at each grade, with the title its grade allows and the atlas record beside it, each name in quotation marks. Documented: The Department of Transportation had spent 46.6 percent of the infrastructure law’s transportation funds by July 31, 2026. Well supported: Local reporting raises incumbents’ risk of losing office. Plausible: Better public services can build earned trust in government, beside the atlas name Better public services build earned trust. Contested: two readings of 15 words each, one finding effects near zero and one finding small drops. Hypothesis: Untested: more expert congressional staff may reduce insider influence.
s-13-2-correct.notes: Every grade and every reading from the atlas's connection records. The two contested readings run 15 words each (Rule 01.16). The Documented row is a count on the public record in LE02's own record, in record words (statistics S1, CD S5).

s-13-2-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A diagram head whose label reads Plausible, some evidence, titled Better public services build earned trust, with the direct verb build and no can or may.
s-13-2-failure.notes: Labeled failure: the atlas's name for L20 used as a title; the label is right (CD M3), so it fails on the verb alone.

s-13-3-correct.alt: The mapping table. Each row gives a display word, its gloss for a key, the grade values our systems atlas stores with their counts, and how a connection draws it. Documented, on the public record: a solid line with the record square. Well supported, strong research evidence, which the atlas spells two ways: a solid line. Plausible, some evidence: a dashed line. Contested, evidence disputed, which covers plausible_contested, contested and the contested flag: dash and dot. Hypothesis, not yet tested: dots. Mixed, on one issue record, and Retired, a record status kept out of keys, draw no line.
s-13-3-correct.notes: Every count read from the atlas by script. Key glosses as Rule 12.6's key prints them (the chart system's GRADE_TABLE); the line names as Rule 10.10 draws them; plausible_contested as Contested, as the atlas concepts mapped it. Tension 8 asked for this table.

s-13-3-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A chart key that lists well_supported and well-supported as two entries, plausible_contested as the atlas stores it, a made-up grade called Strong, and hypothesis in lower case, each beside a line sample.
s-13-3-failure.notes: Labeled failure: the atlas's stored values printed raw, one grade spelled two ways, a homemade grade word.

s-13-4-correct.alt: Four loops from our systems atlas, each with a dark label giving the grade of its least certain step, and each step drawn as a short arrow in the line of its grade, with a sign tag, its typed chip, its name in quotation marks and its grade word. Loop R10, labeled Plausible: two documented steps, each with the record square, one well supported, all solid, and one plausible step, dashed, the loop’s weakest. Loop R16, labeled Hypothesis: a well-supported solid step and an untested step in dots. Loop R3, labeled Contested: a plausible dashed step and a contested step in dash and dot. Loop B2, labeled Well supported: one hollow line, since the atlas gives the loop no numbered connection.
s-13-4-correct.notes: Every line is the atlas build's wire_marks at 2 px (Rule 10.10's builders line), with the oa.chart.grade values the data lead read from it (D3-84); the record square and the hollow line as Gate 1's M1 approved them.

s-13-4-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. Loop R10’s four steps, each drawn as a solid arrow with its chip and name, with no label, no grade word and no record square, so the plausible step looks as firm as the documented ones.
s-13-4-failure.notes: Labeled failure: one solid line for every grade and no grade words.

s-13-5-correct.alt: Reform R-30, More homes allowed by right near jobs, with four properties in four places. Its label reads Plausible, the grade of the evidence that it works. Effect size: one row for each outcome family, with pips beside a zero line and the atlas’s code and words: Quality of democracy +S, small positive, delayed; Government efficacy 0, no expected effect, drawn as a bar on the zero line; Economic performance +M, moderate positive; Income and wealth equality +M, moderate positive, renter-owner. Uncertainty, in the atlas’s words: high where binding; medium for US statutes. Delay: the two connections it targets drawn in red, Connection L39, Owners’ equity drives opposition to new housing, with three ticks for over 10 years, and Connection LE17, Housing scarcity raises rents and prices, with two ticks for 2 to 10 years. A note says the reform acts where the marks turn red and names its third target, Variable A5, housing scarcity.
s-13-5-correct.notes: Pips and the zero bar as Gate 1's M4 effect mark draws them; qualifiers kept as the atlas writes them; no total. The targets take Rule 12.5's red target, the plate's one working red, drawn by wire_marks at the 6 px sizes with a 4 px red line on a 6 px Charcoal case (brand S4, statistics S11).

s-13-5-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. Reform R-30 with an impact score of +5, the four outcome families added together, and a thick bar for the strength of its evidence. No delay appears.
s-13-5-failure.notes: Labeled failure: a total across outcome families, a bar's thickness for a grade, delay left out.

s-13-6-correct.alt: A jobs chart’s head and foot: the grade line Documented: a Bureau of Labor Statistics survey of employers, as copied by FRED, the title The three-month average of monthly job change stood at 51,000 in September 2026, a preliminary figure, its measure line, a note that says what seasonally adjusted means, and the source line, Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics, all nonfarm employees, monthly change, seasonally adjusted, January 2022 to September 2026, United States, via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Retrieved November 6, 2026. August and September 2026 are preliminary and will be revised. A table then takes the line apart: publisher, title or table, observation period, geography, the copy we read, date retrieved and qualification. Under it, a source line for a value from our systems atlas follows the same order.
s-13-6-correct.notes: The source line is the engineer's sidecar printed_source_line for fred-payrolls-monthly-change, read by script, never retyped. The title is level and counts no drops (D3-87, statistics M4); the three-month average, 50.7 thousand, is read from the same file.

s-13-6-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same jobs chart’s head, titled The three-month average of monthly job change stood at 51,000 in September 2026, a preliminary figure, with a short measure line and the source line Source: FRED data.
s-13-6-failure.notes: Labeled failure: a copy named in place of the publisher; no table, period, geography, date or qualification. The grade line is right, so the plate fails on its source line alone.

s-13-7-correct.alt: Two charts shown together, each a chart head over a small line chart in one window, 2009 to 2025, on one scale: Child poverty stood at 13.4 percent in 2025, and Poverty among all people stood at 13.1 percent in 2025. A note gives the shared window and its reason and says that tying a change to a policy takes a study of its own. The source line names children under 18 and all people and the current release. A table sets the two releases side by side for children: 2020, 9.7 before the revision and 9.6 now; 2021, 5.2 and 5.1; 2024, 13.4 and 13.5.
s-13-7-correct.notes: Rows from the engineer's census-spm-child-poverty file; the pair's source line from the sidecar, both groups named; the earlier release's line from the sidecar's variant, its qualification as statistics M3 gives it. The two charts are the kit's line-event-notes form through the guide hook (contract C7).

s-13-7-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. Two charts side by side. The first is titled Child poverty fell from 9.7 percent in 2020 to 5.2 percent in 2021, then rose to 13.5 percent in 2024, with no period or release named. The second, beside it, draws a line that starts in 2017.
s-13-7-failure.notes: Labeled failure: 2020 and 2021 from the earlier release beside 2024 from the current one, with no release named, and two windows in one set.

s-13-8-correct.alt: A story card. Its headline, Medicare caps what Part D enrollees pay for each covered insulin at $35 a month, and the line under it report a real rule, with its source line. An invented reader, Ruth Okafor, 71, of Alder County, says she checks each fall that her insulin is still on her plan’s list, with the Illustrative label beside her name.
s-13-8-correct.notes: The rule and its dates from the atlas's headline figures (checked October 15, 2026); the reader, her words and Alder County are invented. Lora Italic for her words (DR-47).

s-13-8-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same story card with the invented reader and her words unlabeled, and a note at the foot that says some people and quotes in our pieces are illustrative.
s-13-8-failure.notes: Labeled failure: one general note at the foot in place of a label beside the invented reader. The caption names her as invented, so the plate itself carries no label (the failure it shows).

s-13-9-correct.alt: Three sentences, each atlas ID in its typed chip with the record’s name after it. Variable B4, hostility toward the other political party, can raise Variable B6, exposure to hostile political content, through Connection L46. Loop B4, electoral consequences can improve public performance, runs through Variable C3, risk of losing office. Loop R1, wealth and political influence reinforce each other, and Reform R-01, all-party primaries with ranked general elections, are separate records.
s-13-9-correct.notes: Chips as Rule 18.24 builds them (c-18-id-chip); every ID and name read from the atlas; B2 to B5 are the IDs variables and loops share.

s-13-9-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A sentence of bare codes: When B4 rises, B6 can rise with it. B4 runs through C3, and R1 explains why R-01 matters.
s-13-9-failure.notes: Labeled failure: bare atlas IDs, two of them the same code for different kinds of record.

s-13-10-correct.alt: Reform R-19, Rules for drug-pricing middlemen (PBMs), with its status dated as of October 15, 2026: partly in place. A table lists three routes to change. Route FS, Federal statute, feasibility high, checked October 15, 2026. Route ENF, Enforcement and litigation, feasibility medium, not checked. Route SS, State statute, feasibility high, not checked.
s-13-10-correct.notes: Routes, ratings and check dates read from the atlas; 13 of its 126 route entries carry a date.

s-13-10-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. Reform R-19 under the heading Where it stands now, with its three routes and their feasibility and no date on the status or on any route.
s-13-10-failure.notes: Labeled failure: an undated status and routes that read as checked.

s-13-11-correct.alt: Loop R1, wealth and political influence reinforce each other, in two parts. The atlas’s coding note opens the plate: a row’s direction describes the rule’s effect on who officials answer to and carries no judgment of the people or parties involved. Events: the atlas’s seven repair log rows on the loop, labeled Finding, Documented, each a filled shape for its instrument with its date, place and what it did, under headings that say how the atlas codes them. The atlas codes these rows toward voters: New York City’s Local Law 8 in 1988, marked source not checked; New York City’s Charter Question 1 in 2018; Seattle’s Proposition 1 in 2025; Alaska’s Ballot Measure 1 in 2026. The atlas codes these rows away from voters: the court rulings in Citizens United in 2010, McCutcheon in 2014 and NRSC in 2026. None has an arrow. Causal claims, labeled Plausible: the loop’s three connections, drawn as arrows in the line of their grades with sign tags and delay ticks: L01 well supported, L02 plausible, L03 well supported.
s-13-11-correct.notes: Event shapes as Gate 1's M4 approved them: ballot measure a square, statute or local law a wide bar, court ruling a tall bar, executive or agency action a framed square. Each row's words are a short form of the atlas's own. The coding note opens the plate and each heading names the atlas (D3-85, brand M1); all seven rows stay, in date order (D3-86).

s-13-11-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A box for the Citizens United ruling of January 21, 2010 joined by a solid arrow with a plus sign tag to a box for money spent to influence politics, graded Documented with the record square.
s-13-11-failure.notes: Labeled failure: a dated event drawn with the causal grammar of a connection.

s-13-12-correct.alt: A quotation set beside Variable D6, state and local testing of reforms, in our systems atlas. In Lora Italic: “It is one of the happy incidents of the federal system that a single courageous State may, if its citizens choose, serve as a laboratory; and try novel social and economic experiments without risk to the rest of the country.” Under it: Louis D. Brandeis, associate justice of the Supreme Court, dissenting in New State Ice Co. v. Liebmann, an Oklahoma case the Court decided on March 21, 1932. The source line names the case in the United States Reports, page 311, via the Library of Congress, retrieved November 11, 2026.
s-13-12-correct.notes: The words copied from the United States Reports scan at https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/ll/usrep/usrep285/usrep285262/usrep285262.pdf, page 311, read November 11, 2026, with the decision date (March 21, 1932) and the dissent's running head. The Reports print “State”, as the quote does (statistics S10). The opinion holds neither “laboratories” nor “democracy”, which the failure plate's paraphrase uses (checked by script in the scan's text).

s-13-12-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A pull quote in Lora Italic, “States are the laboratories of democracy.”, credited to Louis Brandeis with no role, date, place or source.
s-13-12-failure.notes: Labeled failure: a later paraphrase in quotation marks; the opinion's text holds neither word it turns on.

s-13-13-correct.alt: An invented article and its corrections page entry, each labeled Illustrative. Above the headline, Alder County’s libraries add Sunday hours from January, a note with a dark bar reads: Corrected November 4, 2026. An earlier version of this article and its chart gave the Main Library’s weekly hours as 58. The county’s adopted schedule gives 52. We replaced the chart and fixed the second paragraph. The fixed chart follows, ranking weekly hours: Main Library 52, Riverside 44, Elm Street 36. The corrections page lists the same note under its date, with the headline and the date the article first ran.
s-13-13-correct.notes: Invented throughout, one label at the head of each piece (DR-97). The note's tokens follow Rule 26.3's example for a correction notice: primary text and a 4 px bar in the essential graphic color. The chart is the kit's figure from s-13-13-correct.chart.json (contract C7).

s-13-13-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same invented article, labeled Illustrative, with the chart already showing 52 hours and one word at its foot, Updated, with no date and no account of what was wrong.
s-13-13-failure.notes: Labeled failure: a silent fix with an undated Updated line at the foot.
